title: Titch and the Upside-Down Map
markdown:
Titch was a goblin with eyes that sparkled just like the stars above his home in the sparkly Starfall Highlands, a place where the mountains tickled the clouds and the moon painted everything with silver dust. He lived in a snug little den tucked between rocky hills, a place that always felt warm and safe. And with Titch, always, was his best friend, Squeaky. Squeaky was a tiny mouse, soft as a dandelion puff, with whiskers that wiggled with every new smell. Squeaky loved to ride on Titch’s shoulder, peeking out from under the brim of Titch’s cap. There he’d sit, a little grey puffball, his tiny paws holding tight to Titch’s shirt.

One evening, as the sky turned rosy pink like a sleepy cheek, Titch had a very important job. Old Farmer Bramble, who lived way down in the valley where fluffy white sheep grazed like clouds, had borrowed Titch’s special moon-lantern. Oh, but this wasn't just any old light, you see! A goblin’s moon-lantern is made of shiny silver and special, glittery glass. It catches the moonlight and holds it tight, giving a soft, steady glow that’s just right for seeing your way. It’s like holding a little piece of the moon itself! Titch was to take it back.

Farmer Bramble, a jolly man with a beard as white and fluffy as a dandelion clock and cheeks as red as apples, gave Titch a little rolled-up paper. It felt old and crinkly in Titch’s small hands. “Now, Titch, my boy,” Farmer Bramble boomed, his voice warm and rumbling like a happy tummy. “Follow this map to my farm. It’s not too far, but the paths can get twisty up here, and the shadows like to play games!”

Titch’s pointy ears perked up. He felt so big and important! “I will, Farmer Bramble!” he chirped, his voice as bright as a new penny. Squeaky, snuggled in his spot, gave a tiny, happy squeak, meaning, “We’ll find it together!”

Ah, but this is where the fun begins! The moon was just peeking over the tallest mountain, spreading its soft, silvery light. It made deep, friendly shadows dance all around. Not too far from Titch’s den was the Little Silver Forest. Oh, it was a sight! The trees there had leaves like tiny mirrors, catching the moonlight and throwing it back in playful little twinkles. And the moss on the ground sparkled, as if someone had sprinkled it with diamond dust. It was simply enchanting, truly.

Titch took a few steps down the path, the borrowed lantern swinging gently in his hand. Its soft glow made a little pool of light around his feet. Squeaky twitched his nose, smelling the sweet, earthy smell of the forest floor. “Squeak! Squeak!” he whispered, pointing a tiny paw towards a patch of moss that glowed brighter than all the rest. It looked like a little piece of the starry sky had fallen right there!

Titch’s eyes went wide with wonder. “Oh, Squeaky, look!” he exclaimed with a happy sigh. The moss was like a carpet of tiny, real stars, glowing all by itself. Titch stepped just a little way off the path to get a closer peek. His boots sank a tiny bit into the soft, damp ground. The air smelled like fresh earth and sweet wildflowers. The moonlight made pretty dancing patterns on the ground, and Titch loved to chase them with his eyes. He was so busy looking at the sparkly moss and the way the light played peek-a-boo through the leaves, that he forgot all about Farmer Bramble’s map for a moment.

Now, you see, Farmer Bramble’s map was a very good map, but only if you looked at it just right. It had little pictures of trees and rocks and twisty paths. But Titch, in his excitement, had turned it this way and that, trying to match it to the pretty forest. He’d even tucked it into his pocket for a little while when he was admiring a big, shiny leaf that felt cool and smooth.

He kept walking, humming a happy little goblin song: “Moonbeam, moonbeam, shine so bright, light my path with all your light.” But the path seemed to get smaller, and the trees looked all jumbled up. Titch pulled out his map again. He looked at it, then at the trees, then back at the map. Hmm. Something wasn’t quite right. The wiggly line on the map didn't look like the trees in front of him at all.

Suddenly, Titch stopped. Right in front of him, in a clearing bathed in a soft, warm light, was a tiny cottage. It looked like it was made of yummy gingerbread and happy wishes. A thin puff of smoke curled from its chimney, smelling of warm herbs and sweet, baked apples. And sitting on a little wooden stool outside, tending to a basket bursting with green leaves and colourful flowers – bright pinks, sunny yellows, and deep purples – was a woman. She had kind eyes, a smile that crinkled like a wise old owl, and a long, flowing scarf the colour of a sunset that seemed to dance even when there was no wind. This was a nice witch, my dear child. Not a spooky one, oh no! A kind witch who loved growing things.

She looked up as Titch came closer, his lantern making a friendly glow on the dewy grass. Squeaky, still on Titch’s shoulder, peeked out, his whiskers wiggling with curiosity. “Well now,” she said, her voice like the whisper of leaves on a warm day. “And what have we here? A little goblin and his small friend. You look a bit… wobbly. Have you lost your way?”

Titch felt his goblin cheeks turn pink, like a wild rose. “Um, we were going to Farmer Bramble’s,” he mumbled, holding up the lantern as if it might explain things. “But I think… I think the path got all mixed up. Or maybe we did.”

The witch chuckled, a soft, warm sound that made Titch feel much better. “A little lost, are we? That happens sometimes, especially on such a lovely night. And what’s that you have there?” She pointed to the lantern. “That’s a very pretty moon-lantern. It’s shining so nicely. Are you collecting pieces of the sky, perhaps?”

Titch shook his head, his ears flopping a little. “No, it’s borrowed. I was taking it back to Farmer Bramble. But… my map…” He pulled it out again, sighing as he opened it.

The witch’s eyes twinkled like little stars. “Ah, maps! They can be tricky. Especially when they’re upside down, you see.” She waved a hand that smelled of mint and lavender. “This is Farmer Bramble’s cottage, yes, but you’ve been walking in circles, little one. Your map… well, the top is the bottom, and the bottom is the top!”

Titch looked at the map, then at the witch, and a happy giggle bubbled out of him. “Oh!” he said, his eyes wide. “It *is* upside down!” Squeaky, who had been listening very carefully, gave a loud, clear squeak that sounded like, “I think she’s right!”

The kind witch smiled a big, warm smile. She picked a plump, juicy berry from her basket. It was a deep red and looked delicious. She offered it to Titch. “Here,” she said. “A little treat for your journey. It’s a dreamberry. It will give you sweet dreams. And a little piece of advice: always look twice at your map, and listen to your friends. Sometimes they see things we miss, with their sharp eyes and wiggly noses.” She gently took the map and turned it the right way up. Then, oh my, it made perfect sense! She pointed with a finger that seemed to glow with faint starlight. “Farmer Bramble’s farm is just down *that* way, past the whispering trees and over the little bubbly stream. You’ll be there soon!”

Titch felt a warm, happy feeling spread through him. He thanked the kind witch with all his heart. Squeaky gave a happy wiggle on his shoulder. The moon-lantern in Titch’s hand seemed to shine even brighter now. The path ahead, lit by the witch’s kind words and the perfectly turned map, looked clear and welcoming. Titch waved goodbye to the nice witch. With Squeaky settled happily on his shoulder, Titch set off. The Little Silver Forest still sparkled, but now Titch knew exactly where he was going. His steps were steady and sure. He had his lantern, his best friend, and the happy feeling of a task almost done. Soon, he knew, he would be home, safe and sound, ready for his own cozy bed, dreaming of sparkly moss and kind witches.
characters: Titch the young goblin, a mouse
